title: Despite rising backlash, D.C. robotaxi bill set for council vote
source_used: City Cast DC (full text) and Gadget Review (full text); Axios page blocked
key_facts: Janeese Lewis George, a Ward 4 councilmember and the Democratic nominee for mayor (City Cast DC calls her the presumptive mayor-to-be), said on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 that rushing the legalization of autonomous vehicles is "irresponsible" given expected AI-related job losses.
Since May the D.C. Council has been reviewing a bill that would allow robotaxis, such as Alphabet-owned Waymo, to operate in the District.

Labor unions, about two dozen of which backed Lewis George's campaign, oppose the bill; Brian Wivell of Amalgamated Transit Union Local 689 called autonomous vehicles "anti-public transit embodied in one vehicle".
Waymo has worked with Ward 6 Councilmember Charles Allen to add a workforce support and transition fund to the bill.
Waymo cars with a human in the passenger seat have been mapping the District for years but offer no commercial service there.
City Cast DC says there is no public date for when the bill will next be considered by the council or Allen's transportation committee.

Gadget Review's summary of the bill (not checked against the text): first fleets capped at 200 vehicles, no commercial launch before January 2028, at least $5 million in liability insurance, per-mile fees for Metro and worker transition.
quote_evidence: Presumptive mayor-to-be and Ward 4 Councilmember Janeese Lewis George said Thursday that it would be “irresponsible” to rush legalizing autonomous vehicles, as the D.C. Council considers that exact question.
Since May, the Council has been reviewing a bill that would allow robotaxis, such as those from Alphabet-owned Waymo, to operate in the District.
There is not a public date when the bill will next be considered before the council or Allen’s transportation committee.
why_it_matters_hint: The person most likely to be the next mayor is publicly against moving fast on a robotaxi bill, which could shape the council debate.
event_date: Thursday 15 Oct 2026 (Lewis George statement); Axios piece dated Friday 16 Oct 2026
notes: Axios page blocked (Cloudflare). Axios' headline says the bill is "set for council vote"; City Cast DC on 15 Oct 2026 says no public date is set for its next consideration, and Gadget Review says committee consideration is expected. The vote date could not be confirmed, so the entry does not state one. Bill details from Gadget Review (a gadget news site) are attributed as its summary.
